testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When exiting a bus, a driver must:

options.text: Keep one hand on the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep one hand on the handrail.
questions.explanation: When exiting a bus, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. Keep at least one hand on the handrail at all times. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: One way to prevent drowsiness while driving is to:

options.text: Get enough sleep the night before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get enough sleep the night before you drive.
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is dangerous. To avoid drowsiness, get a full night of sleep before driving, bring a passenger, plan trips during your normal awake hours, and avoid medicines that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise also helps keep you alert while driving.

questions.question: Drowsy driving happens most often at:
questions.correctAnswerText: Night.
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is most common at night because people are naturally less alert during their normal sleep hours. If you must drive at night, take steps to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: What color light shows that ABS is not working?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: A yellow warning light on the dashboard means the ABS system is not working correctly.

questions.question: After you start the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Check your gauges when starting the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds after the engine starts.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect drivers from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
Protect drivers' heads when they enter the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect drivers from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
questions.explanation: A header board protects the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: When backing a trailer:

options.text: You should not back in a straight line.
You should not fix drift until you are far off course.
You should move forward often to reposition the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should move forward often to reposition the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When backing, move forward to reposition your vehicle as needed. Fix any drift right away by turning the steering wheel toward the drift direction.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
It sends air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks in an air brake system. The air compressor governor controls when the compressor runs.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. This air pressure enters when the driver:
questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Is usually more careful than other drivers.
May react slower to dangers than a well-rested driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: May react slower to dangers than a well-rested driver.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers see and react to hazards slower than rested drivers. Fatigue reduces your ability to make quick, critical driving decisions.

questions.question: On a slippery road, what should a driver do?

options.text: Make turns as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass slower vehicles.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Turn gently and avoid passing other vehicles unless necessary.

questions.question: When driving on a surface with poor traction, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To stay in control of the vehicle.
So you do not go faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stay in control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly on wet or snowy roads. This helps you keep control and prevents skidding.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: To tell other drivers you are angry.
To warn other drivers you are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn other drivers you are nearby.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others of your presence. Only use it when necessary because it can startle other drivers.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, what should you never do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Never press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force of the springs and air pressure can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks collect water and compressor oil. These must be drained regularly. If they build up, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.correctAnswerText: Unstable.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable cargo. It swings during transport and has a high center of gravity.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how are air tanks arranged?

options.text: Air tanks are shared between both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They should not be used in cold weather.
They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
They send air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil. These build up in air tanks and can harm the system. Drain valves remove this buildup.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You lose extra points on your final score.
You automatically fail the entire test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire test.
questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and use three points of contact when exiting. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Exit the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to drive off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information at the crossing and call 911 or another emergency number.

questions.question: Water on a roadway can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hydroplaning.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: When parking, do not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: If brakes are hot after going down a steep hill, do not use the parking brake. Let them cool first to avoid damage.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Is probably aware of what is happening around them.
May not be aware of what is happening around them.
Can hear the sounds of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle and could do something dangerous.

questions.question: After an accident, which action is not recommended?

options.text: Moving your vehicle to the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving away from the scene
questions.explanation: After an accident, protect the area, call authorities, help the injured, collect information, and report it. Leaving the scene can cost you your license.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, start by:

options.text: Turning the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
Turning the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When backing a trailer, first turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the wheel direction.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and the one ahead is:

options.text: Not encouraged, as it slows traffic.
Encouraged, as it gives you time to react to hazards.
Only encouraged if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged, as it gives you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to react safely if something goes wrong.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill:

options.text: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
Continuously downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control speed. Use the brakes only as backup.

questions.question: The minimum tire tread depth for rear tires is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. All tires on a vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest speed is:

options.text: The same speed as surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Takes your attention away from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes your attention away from the road.
questions.explanation: Eating while driving is dangerous. It takes your focus off the road and requires you to take one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: When inspecting your tires, you do not want to find:

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.
Valve stems that are not damaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Different tire sizes.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: When should a driver sign a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: After any problems have been fixed

questions.correctAnswerText: After any problems have been fixed
questions.explanation: Sign a vehicle inspection report only if problems were found and either fixed or certified as not needing to be fixed.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you should inspect it:

options.text: Only at the start of the trip.
Only after driving a long distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: After every break.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo and its securing devices before starting. After you begin driving, check within the first 50 miles. Then check every three hours or every 150 miles. Also check after every break.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which of the following?
questions.correctAnswerText: The number of vehicles passed
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the distance traveled and fuel purchased. Required information includes trip dates and total distance traveled. It does not need to include the number of vehicles passed.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look carefully for any leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when rain first starts because:

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Tires are not made for wet weather.
Water has not yet washed away the dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it creates a slick film on the road. This happens because rainwater mixes with oil and grease on the road surface that has not yet washed away.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: You cannot write text, but you can read it.
You can write text, but you cannot read it.
You cannot write or read text.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot write or read text.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial vehicle is not allowed. Texting means typing text into a device or reading text on a device.

questions.question: For a basic vehicle control skills test, you must be able to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Alley dock.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes straight line backing, offset back parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: To ensure normal stopping power, drivers with a front brake limiting valve should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Set the control to normal.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Set the valve to "normal" to keep full stopping power. The "slippery" setting reduces stopping power.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required by law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, no matter how long.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?
questions.correctAnswerText: Water
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must drain the tanks regularly.

questions.question: While going downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph below your safe speed.
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until you reach 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brakes. Repeat this pattern.

questions.question: Not draining air tanks could cause:

options.text: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, you should:

options.text: Hope the vehicle is fine until another driver takes over.
Check it out to find the right solution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check it out to find the right solution.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, get it checked out.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel gap, you should:

options.text: Make sure there is a gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When checking a tractor and trailer connection, look at the fifth wheel gap. Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: If you turn to avoid a hazard:

options.text: You should not brake, as it may lock the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should not brake, as it may lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning quickly to avoid a hazard. Braking could lock the wheels and cause your vehicle to skid out of control.

questions.question: The tread depth on non-front tires of a commercial vehicle should be at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles need 4/32 of an inch tread depth on front tires and 2/32 of an inch on other tires.

questions.question: When should you cancel the turn signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: After the turn is completed
questions.explanation: Keep your signal on throughout the turn. Cancel it only after the turn is done.

questions.question: To use controlled braking, you should:

options.text: Brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying your brakes as hard as possible while keeping the wheels from locking. Use very small steering wheel movements when braking this way.
